summary: A Node require.resolve probe ran outside npx's installed-package resolution context and returned MODULE_NOT_FOUND; exact npm registry fields and the pinned CLI were used instead.
One broad npm metadata query exceeded the output budget; subsequent registry evidence was read one exact field per command.
Several Windows rg probes incorrectly used a wildcard as a literal path operand, and one replacement search was overly broad; later reads used an exact directory plus rg globs or exact files.

The first two pre-dispatch receipts misclassified the disposable non-Git process as an assigned agent worktree; the runtime state was corrected to keep the DeepSeek process in its lane without a Git workspace assignment.

Static config-dump admission missed the adapter runtime invariant that retryableCodes cannot be empty; the sole provider-capable process failed before provider I/O and the result was corrected to a bounded no-call outcome.
One latch edit guessed a full commit id from short commit output; exact git rev-parse readback immediately replaced it.

The first exact recursive cleanup command was rejected by command policy; after preserving the already verified exact target, cleanup used the recoverable Windows Recycle Bin path and absence was read back.
